summary.name: SRE in the Third Age
summary.one_liner: A 2019 SREcon EMEA talk by Björn Rabenstein of Grafana Labs on the history of Site Reliability Engineering and speculation about its possible future.
use_cases: understanding the history of site reliability engineering
reading background on how SRE spread beyond Google
considering how SRE roles may change
summary.what_it_does: ["Describes three eras of SRE: first as a Google-proprietary practice, second as a well-known discipline adopted by many organizations, and a speculative third age.", "Argues the field is nearing the late stage of the second age, citing recruiters using the term SRE in job descriptions.", "Suggests the third age might mean the end of SRE as currently known.", "Includes the speaker's bio: an engineer at Grafana and Prometheus developer, formerly at SoundCloud and Google."]
notable: Talk from SREcon19 EMEA held in Dublin, published by USENIX Association in October 2019
Speaker works at Grafana Labs and develops Prometheus
USENIX Open Access: slides and video posted after the event are free to view
caveats: Page text is a talk abstract and bibliographic entry; no full transcript or slides are included in the text provided
Speculative content about the 'third age' is not a concrete tool or product
